Title: Ojibwe
Chunks: 5,6,7,8,9
According to the U.S. census, Ojibwe people are one of the largest tribal populations among [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") peoples in the U.S. In Canada, they are the second-largest [First Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Nations_in_Canada "First Nations in Canada") population, surpassed only by the [Cree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cree "Cree"). They are one of the most numerous [Indigenous peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") north of the [Rio Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande "Rio Grande").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-3)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] The Ojibwe population is approximately 320,000, with 170,742 living in the U.S. as of 2010 and approximately 160,000 in Canada.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-capop2-1) In the U.S. there are 77,940 mainline Ojibwe, 76,760 Saulteaux, and 8,770 Mississauga, organized in 125 bands. In Canada they live from western [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") to eastern [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia").
The Ojibwe language is [Anishinaabemowin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe_language "Ojibwe language"), a branch of the [Algonquian language family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_languages "Algonquian languages").

The Ojibwe are part of the [Council of Three Fires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Three_Fires "Council of Three Fires") (along with the [Odawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odawa_people "Odawa people") and [Potawatomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi "Potawatomi")) and of the larger Anishinaabeg, which includes [Algonquin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquin_people "Algonquin people"), [Nipissing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nipissing_First_Nation "Nipissing First Nation"), and Oji-Cree people. Historically, through the Saulteaux branch, they were part of the [Iron Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Confederacy "Iron Confederacy"), with the Cree, [Assiniboine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assiniboine "Assiniboine"), and [Metis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9tis "Métis").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-:0-4)

The [dreamcatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamcatcher "Dreamcatcher") originated from the Ojibwe and became a popular commercial item in the late 20th century and became a symbol for the [Pan-Indian movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Indianism "Pan-Indianism").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-5) The Ojibwe are known for their [birchbark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birchbark "Birchbark")[canoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoe "Canoe"), [birchbark scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birchbark_scrolls "Birchbark scrolls"), mining and trade in [copper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper "Copper"), and their harvesting of [wild rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_rice "Wild rice") and [maple syrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maple_syrup "Maple syrup").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-6) Their [Midewiwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midewiwin "Midewiwin") Society is well respected as the keeper of detailed and complex scrolls of events, oral history, songs, maps, memories, stories, geometry, and mathematics.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-7)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]
European powers, Canada, and the U.S. have colonized Ojibwe lands. The Ojibwe signed treaties with settler leaders to share land for the survival of settlers in exchange for compensation, according to Midewiwin laws pre-dating European contact, with an expectation of mutual non-interference. Many European settlers moved into the Ojibwe ancestral lands.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-capop2-1)

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Pf026012.jpg/250px-Pf026012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pf026012.jpg)
Ojibwa women in a canoe at [Leech Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leech_Lake "Leech Lake"), [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota"), in 1909
The [exonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exonym_and_endonym "Exonym and endonym") for this Anishinaabe group is _Ojibwe_ (plural: _Ojibweg_). This word has two variations, one French (Ojibwa) and the other English (Chippewa).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-8) Although [many variations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwa_ethnonyms "Ojibwa ethnonyms") exist in the literature, _Chippewa_ is more common in the United States, and _Ojibway_ predominates in Canada,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-9) but both terms are used in each country. In many Ojibwe communities throughout Canada and the U.S. since the late 20th century, more members have been using the generalized name _Anishinaabe(-g)_.
The meaning of the name _Ojibwe_ is not known; the most common explanations for the name's origin are:

*   _ojiibwabwe_ (/o/ + /jiibw/ + /abwe/), meaning "those who cook/roast until it puckers", referring to their fire-curing of [moccasin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moccasin_(footwear) "Moccasin (footwear)") seams to make them waterproof.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-10) Some 19th century sources say this name described a method of ritual torture that the Ojibwe applied to enemies.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-11)  
*   _ozhibii'iwe_ (/o/ + /zhibii'/ + /iwe/), meaning "those who keep records [of a Vision]", referring to their form of [pictorial writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe_writing_systems "Ojibwe writing systems"), and [pictographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pictograph "Pictograph") used in Midewiwin sacred rites;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-12) or  
*   _ojiibwe_ (/o/ + /jiib/ + /we/), meaning "those who speak stiffly" or "those who stammer", an exonym or name given to them by the [Cree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cree "Cree"), who described the Ojibwe language for its differences from their own.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-13)

Title: Ho-Chunk
Chunks: 11,12,13
[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Winnebago_wigwam.jpg/330px-Winnebago_wigwam.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winnebago_wigwam.jpg)
Winnebago family in 1852

Ho-Chunk [oral history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_tradition "Oral tradition") says they have always lived in their current homelands of Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, and Illinois.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-17) Their [Siouan language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouan_language "Siouan language") indicates common origin with other peoples of this language group. They say their ancestors built the thousands of [effigy mounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effigy_mound "Effigy mound") through Wisconsin and surrounding states[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-18) during the [Late Woodland period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_period "Late Woodland period"). In the Terminal [Late Woodland Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_Period "Late Woodland Period"), the practice of building effigy mounds abruptly ceased with the appearance of the [Oneota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oneota "Oneota") Culture. The Ho-Chunk claim descendancy from both the effigy mound-building Late Woodland cultures and the successor Oneota Culture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-19) The tribe began cultivating [maize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize") at the end of the [Late Woodland period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_period "Late Woodland period"), while they continued to hunt, fish, and gather wild plants. They cultivated [wild rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_rice "Wild rice") (_[Zizania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zizania "Zizania")_ spp.) and harvested sugar from [sugar maple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_maple "Sugar maple") trees.
Dugout canoes found near many small lakes and rivers are prompting new anthropological research projects near [Madison, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison,_Wisconsin "Madison, Wisconsin"), that may yield better information about ancient settlements.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-20)

### European contact and tribe split
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ho-Chunk&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: European contact and tribe split")]
European contact came in 1634 with the arrival of French explorer [Jean Nicolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Nicolet "Jean Nicolet"). He wrote that the Winnebago/Ho-Chunk occupied the area around Green Bay of [Lake Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan "Lake Michigan") in Wisconsin, reaching beyond Lake Winnebago to the [Wisconsin River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_River "Wisconsin River") and to the [Rock River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_River_(Illinois) "Rock River (Illinois)") in [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"). The oral history also indicates that in the mid-16th century, the influx of [Ojibwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe "Ojibwe") peoples in the northern portion of their lands caused the Ho-Chunk to move to the south of their territory. They had some friction with the tribes of the [Illinois Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Confederacy "Illinois Confederacy") as well as fellow [Chiwere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiwere_language "Chiwere language")-speaking peoples splitting from the Ho-Chunk. These groups, who became the [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_people "Iowa people"), [Missouria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouria "Missouria"), and [Otoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otoe "Otoe") tribes, moved south and west because the reduced range made it difficult for such a large population to be sustained.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-autogenerated1-21)

Historically, through the Saulteaux branch, they were part of the [Iron Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Confederacy "Iron Confederacy"), with the Cree, [Assiniboine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assiniboine "Assiniboine"), and [Metis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9tis "Métis").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-:0-4)
texts.7:
The [dreamcatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamcatcher "Dreamcatcher") originated from the Ojibwe and became a popular commercial item in the late 20th century and became a symbol for the [Pan-Indian movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Indianism "Pan-Indianism").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-5) The Ojibwe are known for their [birchbark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birchbark "Birchbark")[canoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoe "Canoe"), [birchbark scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birchbark_scrolls "Birchbark scrolls"), mining and trade in [copper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper "Copper"), and their harvesting of [wild rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_rice "Wild rice") and [maple syrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maple_syrup "Maple syrup").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-6) Their [Midewiwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midewiwin "Midewiwin") Society is well respected as the keeper of detailed and complex scrolls of events, oral history, songs, maps, memories, stories, geometry, and mathematics.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-7)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]
European powers, Canada, and the U.S. have colonized Ojibwe lands. The Ojibwe signed treaties with settler leaders to share land for the survival of settlers in exchange for compensation, according to Midewiwin laws pre-dating European contact, with an expectation of mutual non-interference. Many European settlers moved into the Ojibwe ancestral lands.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-capop2-1)
texts.8:
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Pf026012.jpg/250px-Pf026012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pf026012.jpg)
Ojibwa women in a canoe at [Leech Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leech_Lake "Leech Lake"), [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota"), in 1909
The [exonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exonym_and_endonym "Exonym and endonym") for this Anishinaabe group is _Ojibwe_ (plural: _Ojibweg_). This word has two variations, one French (Ojibwa) and the other English (Chippewa).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-8) Although [many variations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwa_ethnonyms "Ojibwa ethnonyms") exist in the literature, _Chippewa_ is more common in the United States, and _Ojibway_ predominates in Canada,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-9) but both terms are used in each country. In many Ojibwe communities throughout Canada and the U.S. since the late 20th century, more members have been using the generalized name _Anishinaabe(-g)_.
The meaning of the name _Ojibwe_ is not known; the most common explanations for the name's origin are:
texts.9:
*   _ojiibwabwe_ (/o/ + /jiibw/ + /abwe/), meaning "those who cook/roast until it puckers", referring to their fire-curing of [moccasin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moccasin_(footwear) "Moccasin (footwear)") seams to make them waterproof.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-10) Some 19th century sources say this name described a method of ritual torture that the Ojibwe applied to enemies.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-11)  
*   _ozhibii'iwe_ (/o/ + /zhibii'/ + /iwe/), meaning "those who keep records [of a Vision]", referring to their form of [pictorial writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe_writing_systems "Ojibwe writing systems"), and [pictographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pictograph "Pictograph") used in Midewiwin sacred rites;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-12) or  
*   _ojiibwe_ (/o/ + /jiib/ + /we/), meaning "those who speak stiffly" or "those who stammer", an exonym or name given to them by the [Cree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cree "Cree"), who described the Ojibwe language for its differences from their own.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe#cite_note-13)

texts.12:
Ho-Chunk [oral history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_tradition "Oral tradition") says they have always lived in their current homelands of Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, and Illinois.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-17) Their [Siouan language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouan_language "Siouan language") indicates common origin with other peoples of this language group. They say their ancestors built the thousands of [effigy mounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effigy_mound "Effigy mound") through Wisconsin and surrounding states[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-18) during the [Late Woodland period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_period "Late Woodland period"). In the Terminal [Late Woodland Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_Period "Late Woodland Period"), the practice of building effigy mounds abruptly ceased with the appearance of the [Oneota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oneota "Oneota") Culture. The Ho-Chunk claim descendancy from both the effigy mound-building Late Woodland cultures and the successor Oneota Culture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-19) The tribe began cultivating [maize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize") at the end of the [Late Woodland period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Woodland_period "Late Woodland period"), while they continued to hunt, fish, and gather wild plants. They cultivated [wild rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_rice "Wild rice") (_[Zizania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zizania "Zizania")_ spp.) and harvested sugar from [sugar maple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_maple "Sugar maple") trees.
Dugout canoes found near many small lakes and rivers are prompting new anthropological research projects near [Madison, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison,_Wisconsin "Madison, Wisconsin"), that may yield better information about ancient settlements.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-20)
texts.13:
### European contact and tribe split
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ho-Chunk&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: European contact and tribe split")]
European contact came in 1634 with the arrival of French explorer [Jean Nicolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Nicolet "Jean Nicolet"). He wrote that the Winnebago/Ho-Chunk occupied the area around Green Bay of [Lake Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan "Lake Michigan") in Wisconsin, reaching beyond Lake Winnebago to the [Wisconsin River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_River "Wisconsin River") and to the [Rock River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_River_(Illinois) "Rock River (Illinois)") in [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"). The oral history also indicates that in the mid-16th century, the influx of [Ojibwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ojibwe "Ojibwe") peoples in the northern portion of their lands caused the Ho-Chunk to move to the south of their territory. They had some friction with the tribes of the [Illinois Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Confederacy "Illinois Confederacy") as well as fellow [Chiwere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiwere_language "Chiwere language")-speaking peoples splitting from the Ho-Chunk. These groups, who became the [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_people "Iowa people"), [Missouria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouria "Missouria"), and [Otoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otoe "Otoe") tribes, moved south and west because the reduced range made it difficult for such a large population to be sustained.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho-Chunk#cite_note-autogenerated1-21)

**Hannibal Hamlin** (August 27, 1809 – July 4, 1891) was an American politician and diplomat who was the 15th [vice president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"), serving from 1861 to 1865, during President [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln")'s first term. He was the first [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") vice president.

As an attorney from [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), Hamlin began his political career as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") in the Maine House of Representatives before being elected twice to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), and then to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). With his strong [abolitionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionist "Abolitionist") views, he left the Democratic Party for the newly formed Republican Party in 1856. In the [1860 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election "1860 United States presidential election"), Hamlin balanced the successful Republican ticket as a New Englander partnered with the Midwesterner Lincoln. Although not a close friend of the president, he lent loyal support to his key projects such as the [Emancipation Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation "Emancipation Proclamation") during the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War").
In the [1864 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1864_United_States_presidential_election "1864 United States presidential election"), Hamlin was replaced as vice-presidential nominee by [Andrew Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Johnson "Andrew Johnson"), a [Southern Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Democrats "Southern Democrats") from [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") who remained loyal to the union, and chosen for his appeal to [Southern Unionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Unionists "Southern Unionists"). After being appointed Collector of the Port of Boston, Hamlin was elected to two more terms in the Senate, and finally served as [U.S. Minister to Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Spain "List of ambassadors of the United States to Spain") before retiring in 1882.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg/250px-Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg)
Hamlin c.late 1840s
Hamlin was born to Cyrus Hamlin and Anna ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Livermore) in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_Maine "Paris, Maine") (now in [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), then a part of [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts")). He was a sixth-generation descendant of English colonist James Hamlin, who had settled in [Barnstable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnstable,_Massachusetts "Barnstable, Massachusetts"), part of the [Plymouth Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Colony "Plymouth Colony") in 1639.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-1) He was a grandnephew of U.S. Senator [Samuel Livermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Livermore "Samuel Livermore") II[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-lifeandtimes-2) of New Hampshire.
According to folklore, Hamlin's life was saved when he was an infant by a [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States")[medicine woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine_man "Medicine man") named [Molly Ockett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molly_Ockett "Molly Ockett"). Hamlin was gravely ill, and Ockett prescribed that he be given warm cow's milk, after which he recovered.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-:0-3)

Everyone knows that Maine’s own Hannibal Hamlin ascended to the seat of the American Vice Presidency. But, not that many recall that Hamlin was not the only Maine born man to become Vice President of the United States of America.
On August 9th of 1974, the 37th President of the United States of America, Richard M. Nixon, ended his term as the American Executive in disgrace by resigning his tenure in office nearly half-way thru his second term in the White House.

When he did, his scandal ridden presidency had come to an abrupt end and his second Vice President, Gerald R. Ford, became the 38th President of the United States.
Ford inherited an America that was suffering on many social, political, and economic fronts. The war in Vietnam had officially entered its 18th year and America’s involvement had caused a divisive rift in an explosive society that was being further inflamed by racial violence in the larger inner cities.
The American economy was in a complete shambles and the United States and all of North America was experiencing a severe petroleum shortage that saw lengthy lines at service stations, and strict fuel rationing was forced on customers from coast to coast.
President Ford faced a number of very serious problems and one of them was who to nominate to fill the position of Vice President of the United States, a position he himself had vacated when he was sworn in as President. Ford quickly settled on one man to fill the post, and that man was born in the Pine Tree State.
Nelson Aldrich Rockefeller was born on July 8th of 1908 at Fernwalk, a family home located at 47 Wayman Lane in Bar Harbor. His mother was New England native Abigail Greene Aldrich of Rhode Island, and Nelson’s father was John D. Rockefeller Jr., the wealthy industrialist and son of Standard Oil founder and petroleum tycoon John D. Rockefeller.

Nelson was raised in wealth and luxury and he had spent most of his summers on the estates at Bar Harbor and at Seal Harbor. By June of 1930, the 22-year old Nelson had met a 23-year old Mary Todhunter Clark at Seal Harbor and the two were married.
By 1940, Nelson began his life of public service in the democratic administration of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt by serving as a coordinator of Inter American Affairs in South America. He then served as an Assistant Secretary of State in 1944.
While serving in FDR's administration many began referring to Nelson by is nickname, Rocky.
Rockefeller then accepted appointment as the Nation’s very first Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare, in which role he served from 1953 until 1954 when he then became a Special assistant to republican President Dwight D. Eisenhower, from 1954 to 1955.
By 1959, Nelson Rockefeller ran for and won election as the 49th Governor of New York, a position in which he held for fifteen-years, from 1959 until December 18th of 1974, when President Gerald R. Ford’s nomination of Rockefeller for Vice President was confirmed.

When he did, his scandal ridden presidency had come to an abrupt end and his second Vice President, Gerald R. Ford, became the 38th President of the United States.
Ford inherited an America that was suffering on many social, political, and economic fronts. The war in Vietnam had officially entered its 18th year and America’s involvement had caused a divisive rift in an explosive society that was being further inflamed by racial violence in the larger inner cities.
The American economy was in a complete shambles and the United States and all of North America was experiencing a severe petroleum shortage that saw lengthy lines at service stations, and strict fuel rationing was forced on customers from coast to coast.
President Ford faced a number of very serious problems and one of them was who to nominate to fill the position of Vice President of the United States, a position he himself had vacated when he was sworn in as President. Ford quickly settled on one man to fill the post, and that man was born in the Pine Tree State.
Nelson Aldrich Rockefeller was born on July 8th of 1908 at Fernwalk, a family home located at 47 Wayman Lane in Bar Harbor. His mother was New England native Abigail Greene Aldrich of Rhode Island, and Nelson’s father was John D. Rockefeller Jr., the wealthy industrialist and son of Standard Oil founder and petroleum tycoon John D. Rockefeller.

Nelson was raised in wealth and luxury and he had spent most of his summers on the estates at Bar Harbor and at Seal Harbor. By June of 1930, the 22-year old Nelson had met a 23-year old Mary Todhunter Clark at Seal Harbor and the two were married.
By 1940, Nelson began his life of public service in the democratic administration of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt by serving as a coordinator of Inter American Affairs in South America. He then served as an Assistant Secretary of State in 1944.
While serving in FDR's administration many began referring to Nelson by is nickname, Rocky.
Rockefeller then accepted appointment as the Nation’s very first Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare, in which role he served from 1953 until 1954 when he then became a Special assistant to republican President Dwight D. Eisenhower, from 1954 to 1955.
By 1959, Nelson Rockefeller ran for and won election as the 49th Governor of New York, a position in which he held for fifteen-years, from 1959 until December 18th of 1974, when President Gerald R. Ford’s nomination of Rockefeller for Vice President was confirmed.

**Hannibal Hamlin** (August 27, 1809 – July 4, 1891) was an American politician and diplomat who was the 15th [vice president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"), serving from 1861 to 1865, during President [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln")'s first term. He was the first [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") vice president.
texts.4:
As an attorney from [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), Hamlin began his political career as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") in the Maine House of Representatives before being elected twice to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), and then to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). With his strong [abolitionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionist "Abolitionist") views, he left the Democratic Party for the newly formed Republican Party in 1856. In the [1860 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election "1860 United States presidential election"), Hamlin balanced the successful Republican ticket as a New Englander partnered with the Midwesterner Lincoln. Although not a close friend of the president, he lent loyal support to his key projects such as the [Emancipation Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation "Emancipation Proclamation") during the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War").
In the [1864 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1864_United_States_presidential_election "1864 United States presidential election"), Hamlin was replaced as vice-presidential nominee by [Andrew Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Johnson "Andrew Johnson"), a [Southern Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Democrats "Southern Democrats") from [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") who remained loyal to the union, and chosen for his appeal to [Southern Unionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Unionists "Southern Unionists"). After being appointed Collector of the Port of Boston, Hamlin was elected to two more terms in the Senate, and finally served as [U.S. Minister to Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Spain "List of ambassadors of the United States to Spain") before retiring in 1882.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg/250px-Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Younger_Hannibal_Hamlin.jpg)

Hamlin was born to Cyrus Hamlin and Anna ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Livermore) in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_Maine "Paris, Maine") (now in [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), then a part of [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts")). He was a sixth-generation descendant of English colonist James Hamlin, who had settled in [Barnstable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnstable,_Massachusetts "Barnstable, Massachusetts"), part of the [Plymouth Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Colony "Plymouth Colony") in 1639.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-1) He was a grandnephew of U.S. Senator [Samuel Livermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Livermore "Samuel Livermore") II[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-lifeandtimes-2) of New Hampshire.
According to folklore, Hamlin's life was saved when he was an infant by a [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States")[medicine woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine_man "Medicine man") named [Molly Ockett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molly_Ockett "Molly Ockett"). Hamlin was gravely ill, and Ockett prescribed that he be given warm cow's milk, after which he recovered.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin#cite_note-:0-3)

Iowa’s river systems flow across gently rolling plains and fertile farmland, with most waterways draining into the Mississippi and Missouri rivers. The state is bordered by these two major rivers, while interior rivers like the Des Moines and Cedar play an important role in agriculture and local water supply. Northern and central regions feature smaller tributaries, while southern areas have wider river valleys.
